title: Finite purity coefficient square in exceptional tower coordinates
statement: Fix finite-field datum D, ell≠char(D), finite E/Q_ell and a smooth f=j≫p:X→Y of relative dimension d between separated finite-type Noetherian schemes over its geometric field, with j open and p proper. Use the canonical evaluation and output comparisons [def-sp-purity-reduction-comparisons] and arbitrary supplied gluing data [det-sp-tower-gluing]. Let K be any uniform constructible finite-Tor tower. Give, at each positive level, an ordinary diagonal geometry and an isomorphism alpha from the dualizing complex to the ordered shifted Tate line. For m≤n assume precisely OrientationNormalized at these two levels [def-pur-finite-smooth-canonical-maps]. Give a generator-normalized coefficient line comparison e and an arrow r whose origin equation identifies it with the actual input reduction. Let beta_i be reductionSite of ordinary finite gamma(alpha_i), followed by finiteRightComparison inverse and targetComparison(i). Then scalar extension of beta_n followed by the actual exceptional output reduction equals the site/scalar comparison, reductionSite of pullbackTwistComparison(e) followed by puritySource(r), and beta_m. No tower gamma or pullbackTower reduction is used or assumed, and only the two normalized finite orientations are needed.

source.place: (3), actual pullback and exceptional reductions and coefficient compatibility

proof.text: Apply finite_orientation_reduction to the two normalized inverse orientations. Geometry is a proposition, hence the geometric witnesses agree. Tensor compatibility of the counit mate gives finite purity coefficient compatibility; equivalently transport reductionCompatibilities_purity through the common-exponent Kummer identifications. Apply finite purity naturality at r and paste. Transport by reductionSiteScalarIso. The unique counit-preserving right-adjoint comparisons identify the ordinary exceptional coefficient mate with coefficientMate. Substitute the input-origin equation and Levels.reduction, then cancel the origin and realization comparisons to obtain the stated beta square.
